key_insight: Dilute yttrium solutes and Y2O3 dispersions trap vacancies in Ni-Mo alloys, suppressing defect mobility and thereby improving resistance to molten-salt corrosion.
engineering_relevance: Point-defect engineering offers a practical alloy-design route for extending structural material lifetime in aggressive fluoride-salt environments such as advanced molten salt reactors.
method: DFT calculated vacancy–Y binding and migration barriers.
SCMF diffusion and impurity-trapping models estimated effective vacancy transport.
Corrosion tests compared NM, NMY, and NMYO alloys in molten fluoride salt at 750°C.
evidence_signal: The corrosion ranking matched the transport model: weight loss dropped from 0.52% for NM to 0.23% for NMY and 0.09% for NMYO, with penetration decreasing in the same order.
watch_item: The benefit depends on stable, well-dispersed Y/Y2O3 trap sites; performance may change if microstructure, trap density, or operating conditions differ from the tested state.
paper_title: Role of defect trapping in the enhanced corrosion resistance of Ni-Mo alloys with yttrium and yttrium oxide additions
